correctness.rationale: For Hurwitz Metzler \(A\), \(M=I-hA/2\) is a nonsingular M-matrix, so \(M^{-1}\ge0\) and the Tustin map is \(2M^{-1}-I\). This proves the exact all-dimensional resolvent-diagonal criterion. In two states, direct inversion leaves only two quadratic diagonal inequalities whose conjunction is \(lpha^2-|a-d|lpha-\Delta\ge0\), yielding the stated \(h_\star\). The diagonal counterexample exactly satisfies the published determinant condition while violating the true criterion. The packaged exact-rational verifier independently checks the counterexample, a coupled boundary example, and the resolvent identity.

value.rationale: Tustin discretization is a standard stability-preserving time discretization for continuous-time systems, while entrywise positivity is essential when states represent populations, concentrations, probabilities, or other nonnegative quantities. The finding corrects an explicit published sufficiency statement, supplies the exact safe sampling interval, and shows that interaction can make the conservative diagonal bound arbitrarily pessimistic. The general resolvent-diagonal criterion also isolates exactly where positivity can fail in higher dimension.
